title: Human Behavior Analysis: A Comprehensive Survey on Techniques, Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
authors: Essahraui, S.; Laamriss, I.; Maleh, Y.; ElMakkaoui, K.; Filali, M.; Ouahbi, I.; Abdel-Latif, A.A.; Mousa, M.; Rodrigues, J.J.P.C.
tldr: Comprehensive survey of Human Behavior Analysis (HBA) covering techniques, applications, challenges, and future directions across healthcare, marketing, education, workplace productivity, and criminal justice domains.
problem_and_motivation: Existing surveys on Human Behavior Analysis focus on narrow subdomains like Human Activity Recognition or behavior modeling in isolated contexts. There is a lack of comprehensive studies that cover the entire scope of HBA across multiple application domains and integrate emerging technologies like edge computing and Large Language Models.
approach: Conducted systematic literature review of 202 relevant papers across eight core HBA domains.
Analyzed papers from leading academic databases (IEEE Xplore, ACM, Scopus, Web of Science, etc.) published between 2020-2024.
Applied keyword-based search strategy with terms including 'Human Behavior Analysis', 'Behavioral Modeling', 'Behavior Prediction', and domain-specific terms.
Categorized traditional and modern techniques from manual observation to AI-driven methods.
Explored data sources including sensor data, social media data, physiological signals, and multimodal analysis.
findings: Human Activity Recognition emerged as the most represented area with 47 papers (33 articles, 14 proceedings).
Criminal Justice and Public Safety followed with 36 papers (24 articles, 5 proceedings, 7 preprints).
Healthcare and Mental Health and Workplace Productivity each yielded 18 papers.
Marketing and Consumer Behavior presented 17 papers (13 articles, 4 proceedings).
Modern HBA leverages AI, ML, DL, NLP, and computer vision for real-time, scalable analysis.
Key challenges include data privacy, generalization, real-time processing, and scalability.
Emerging trends include edge computing, Large Language Models, and privacy-preserving techniques.

definitions.definition: An interdisciplinary field combining psychology, sociology, AI, and data science to model, understand, and predict human actions, reactions, and interactions across diverse domains.
Regular and predictable actions exhibited by individuals or groups over time, detected through observation, data collection, and analysis.
Mental processes involved in gaining knowledge and understanding, including memory, attention, perception, and decision-making.
Human emotions such as happiness, sadness, fear, or anger that play a critical role in influencing behavior and can be analyzed through facial expressions, speech, and physiological responses.
Integration of multiple data sources (wearables, video feeds, social interactions, environmental sensors) to create a comprehensive picture of human behavior.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This comprehensive survey addresses gaps in existing literature by providing a holistic review of Human Behavior Analysis across eight core domains. The key contributions include: (1) systematic analysis of 202 papers from 2020-2024, (2) coverage of both traditional and modern AI-driven techniques, (3) identification of key challenges including privacy, generalization, and scalability, and (4) highlighting emerging trends like edge computing and LLMs. The survey provides a roadmap for advancing HBA in both theory and practice.

Criminal Justice and Public Safety followed with 36 papers.
Modern HBA leverages AI, ML, DL, NLP, and computer vision for real-time analysis.

Emerging trends include edge computing, Large Language Models, and privacy-preserving techniques.
limits: Survey focuses on papers from 2020-2024, potentially missing earlier foundational work.
The breadth of coverage may limit depth in any single application domain.
Rapid evolution of AI technologies may require frequent updates to the survey.
Some application domains like financial decision-making have fewer papers (20) compared to others.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 8.A received high relevance as HBA includes anomaly detection. Domain 12.A received high relevance for comprehensive evaluation frameworks. Domains 6.A, 4.A, and 11.A received medium relevance for their connections to financial behavior analysis, existing systems, and user engagement. Other domains were considered but rejected as the survey covers broad HBA applications rather than specific personal finance implementations.
